| [CLAIM-165](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-165.md) v2 | A combined form constituted by mutual entrainment is not thereby a self in the subject sense: two dancers in phase are one coordination, an autonomous process, and still two subjects | The record's own objection to [CLAIM-172](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md), narrowed in version 2 after the owner's reply ([CLAIM-175](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md)). It concedes that the dancing pair is a combined form and an autonomous process. It holds only that nothing in the coupling makes that form a subject, which [ADR-024](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-024.md) reserves "self" for. Open: whether that is the sense of "self" worth asking about is itself in question. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md) v2 | A lower-level collective within the composite person, such as the gut microbiome, can at times drive higher-level behaviour and even experience: the routes exist and the effects are causal in rodents, while the human evidence is modest | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11: "'who drives' isn't a constant. Considering myself as a multi-level agent, part of my composition is my microbiome ... that lower level collective is capable of influencing my higher level behavior and even phenomenological experience." The time claim is filed as the owner's. The microbiome claim is grounded in two reviews read the same day. The routes exist, and the effects are causal in rodents. The human evidence is modest: associations, small effects on subjective stress, and nulls. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-167](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-167.md) | One-way drive rightly passes the threshold criterion: a metronome and its musician, or a nerve and its muscle, form one system relative to a target that needs both, and the direction of coupling gives the system's internal architecture, not its membership | The owner's challenge to the open objection, 2026-10-11: "a metronome driving a musician, or a nerve driving a muscle, passes — and why shouldn't they?" Three reasons, set out by the assistant and accepted for filing by the owner. First, the objection repeats the coupling-constitution worry that [CLAIM-172](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) had already set aside: the criterion makes a new system, not parthood in the organism. Second, its intuitions are about agency, which [QUESTION-035](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md) keeps apart. Third, whether a one-way driver is inside the block or an input is a choice relative to the target. Direction tells peers from hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-168](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-168.md) | Identifying agents by their will-organization is circular: will-organization is defined for an agent already given, and the agent-versus-device comparison presupposes an identified system, so neither can produce the factorization it is meant to find | The record's anticipated objection to the owner's thesis. [TERM-023](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md) is "agent-indexed": a role in an agent already warranted. The will paper supposes its agent ([CLAIM-080](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-080.md)) so as not to face [CLAIM-010](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-010.md). Orseau et al.'s formal agent-device comparison likewise "assume[s] a clearly identified system". To identify agents by will-organization reverses an order of explanation that was chosen deliberately. Open: [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) replies that the test is run on candidate factors, not on agents. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-169](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-169.md) v2 | On Ainslie's account the population of interests is produced by desynchronized valuation, not given by a fixed architecture: an agent is many interests over a choice only as far as its valuations of that choice cross within the choice's horizon | The record's reading of [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md), made in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11. Interests are individuated by the delay at which each dominates, so where curves do not cross there is nothing to individuate them. The self's intertemporal multiplicity is then a variable, not a constant. It does not say that all multiplicity of self is intertemporal. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md) v4 | The agents in a system are a factorization of it relative to a level of description and a target; agents in general are identified by adaptation, and willed agents are individuated by their will-organization: a willed agent is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11, stated in the record's terms after discussion. It is a collaboration, so it is not a quotation: "the agents in a given system are how we factorize that system relative to a given level of description", and agents are "identified by their will (and/or will-organization)". In the discussion, the owner chose will-organization over operative will, in the form "jurisdiction of a will-organization". Operative will flickers with the drive profile; a will-organization is maintained. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-171](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-171.md) | A stored text means only what its readings make of it: the writer's projected receiver is one more reading, so an unread text has possible meanings and no fixed one | The record's anticipated reception-side objection to the owner's storage claim. Its nearest support in the line is [CLAIM-111](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md), a text supporting a distribution over possible communicative situations. No reception theory is held or read. Open: the reply (the joke changed for the reader, not in what it was made to do) works only if the writer's frame is itself recoverable, and that is [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md)'s problem. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-172](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) v9 | Mutual entrainment is a sufficient mark of a combined form, and marks it as one of peers: when each side adjusts the other's timing the pair carries a collective variable neither has alone; one-way drive also makes a combined form, with a hierarchical architecture | The record's reading in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11, "connect extended self to entrainment". Clark & Chalmers' marks of extension are availability marks, and the coupling-constitution objection says coupling does not entail parthood. Mutual entrainment sidesteps the objection rather than answering it: it individuates a new system by its collective variable. It does not cover a passive store like Otto's notebook, which is coupled across time by writing and reading, not by timing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) v7 | A candidate factor is an agent at a level when it is one system there, when a goal-directed description beats a device description by more than the Occam cost, and when its policy would adapt if its actions' consequences changed; it is a willed agent when, further, a will-organization over several regimes describes it better than none, and what passes that is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The assistant's admission test for the owner's thesis, filed at the owner's request. It has three tests on a candidate factor, at a level and for a target. (1) System: it clears the threshold criterion. (2) Description: a model in which it governs its own regimes for goals beats a device model by more than the Occam cost (Orseau et al., priced as in [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)). (3) Adaptation: its governance would change if its actions' consequences changed (Kenton et al.). It answers the circularity objection by running on candidates whose boundaries come from (1), not from agency, and it answers the permissiveness objection without the will paper's supposition. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-176](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md) v4 | Recurrence is the trigger of persistence this record is built around: coding a thing the second time it turns up captures exactly the drift that defeats an argument, and keeps capture from flooding the record | The filing rule of [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) ("a thing gets a code the second time it turns up"), read as one trigger of persistence ([CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md)), and the one this record is built around. Narrowed to that on 2026-10-11, on the owner's reframing. The same threshold appears in three places in luria and was found independently each time. Proposed: the rule has been applied, but no other threshold has been compared with it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-178](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-178.md) v2 | A manuscript should be a view over the argument and not its only copy: a draft written straight from an exchange drops commitments and changes its thesis without saying so, and both become visible only against a record where claims carry status and inclusion separately | Luria's distinction between sources and generated views, carried over from files to argument. The evidence is the two "crystallized arguments" of the What Survives Translation? exchange and the manuscripts drafted from them (workbench 2026/10/09/025539, 2026/10/10/040457). Proposed: the record is kept beside the manuscript, and nothing generates a manuscript from it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-179](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-179.md) v3 | When an agent does the filing, the cost of capturing argument falls on the party that would otherwise pay to re-derive it, which removes the disparity that design-rationale systems were abandoned over | The answer to the cautionary literature the owner filed before the argument schemes were built ([ADR-030](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-030.md)): design rationale goes uncaptured because whoever captures it is not whoever benefits. [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) noted that agent filing changes the risk from capture stopping to capture flooding. This claim states why. Proposed: the record has run for one week. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-180](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-180.md) v3 | Drift is retrieval failure outside a critical distance: a restatement close enough to an idea retrieves it, one that has drifted too far is taken for new, and a code bypasses retrieval by content altogether | Proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11, when the owner raised sparse distributed memory and Hebbian learning after [CLAIM-182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md), and filed at the owner's request. It reads the drift of [CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) through SDM's critical distance (read in [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md)) and Hopfield's basins of attraction (unread when filed; read 2026-10-14 in NOTE-819). The analogy is the claim; whether restatement distance predicts re-derivation has not been measured. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) v3 | The record fixes the grammar an argument is expressed in, though not its shape: its closed vocabulary of schemes, roles and relations formalizes early, and a move that fits no CLAIM, TERM, ARG or declared relation is forced into one or lost until the misfit is noticed and the grammar amended to hold it | Shipman and Marshall's objection to formal representation ([LIT-756](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-756.md)), turned on this record, and narrowed on the owner's correction of 2026-10-11. As the assistant first put it ("a crystal takes the shape of its seed"), it was wrong about crystals. A seed templates the lattice, but the habit is set by growth conditions. The objection therefore reaches the grammar of the argument, and not which claims it comes to hold. Some evidence for it is already in the record: the flourishes it declined to code, and the literature roles that "recurred" but stay in prose ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md) v2 | Storage is not anchoring, addressability is: a structure that is kept but cannot be pointed at part by part does not stop re-derivation, and the same content becomes an anchor once its parts get addresses | An answer to [QUESTION-038](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-038.md), proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's request. The evidence is in the record already: the two shared transcripts persisted throughout, and ideas were re-derived inside them anyway. Their moves became citable only when the workbench reconstructions gave each turn a label. Two exchanges, and the comparison is not controlled, so Proposed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-183](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-183.md) v2 | Generated views of the record, fed back into the exchange, become instruments of the argument: they show where its terms evolved faster than its formalism | From U40 of the translation exchange, the first time a generated view went back into the conversation (workbench 2026/10/10/040455). The assistant read the term-revisions chain as evidence about the manuscript, and made five moves in reply. One of them was "Nucleation itself is a case study". One instance, so Proposed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-184](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-184.md) v3 | Anchors entrench: a structure that persists early can lock in its framing, so that later structure grows on it and alternatives become hard to reach, and retirement by status is the record's remedy only if superseded anchors stop attracting new structure | The cost side of the owner's reframing ([CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md)), proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's request. If persistence is what lets structure grow, it also lets early framings grow structure that is costly to undo. Grounded on Dunitz & Bernstein (unread) and Ostwald (read). The test: do Superseded entries keep drawing new citations? | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) v3 | The nucleation threshold of an argument is whatever makes a structure persist: a persistent structure is available as an anchor, and more complex structure can evolve only on anchors | The owner's reframing of 2026-10-11, after two readings showed that no physical nucleation threshold is a count. The threshold is not recurrence as such but whatever triggers persistence. Recurrence is the trigger this record is built around ([CLAIM-176](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md)), and there are others. The readings fit the reframing: a physical nucleus is defined by persistence, and seeds that do not persist lose their power. Proposed: the generalization is stated, not tested. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-186](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md) v4 | How fast an argument grows sets how it grows: drift tracks how fast new material arrives relative to how fast it is anchored, so a fast, prolific exchange branches, as a crystal grown far from equilibrium does, and a project memory stabilizes an argument by keeping anchoring up with arrival | Proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11, while correcting its own crystal analogy ([CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md)), and filed at the owner's request rather than on a second occurrence. The analogy is to morphological instability. Near equilibrium a growing crystal faces over, and far from it the faces branch. The evidence so far is anecdotal. The fastest stretch of the translation exchange carried two moves of thesis, and drift has not been measured against pace. There is no slow exchange to compare it with, so the claim is Proposed and untested. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-187](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-187.md) v2 | Whether two systems compute the same way can be tested by quotienting the full admissible symmetry group and measuring what remains: a residual barrier marks a different mechanism, and a feature with no counterpart blocks the comparison | The record's one fully measured case of "factor out the admissible symmetries, then test what survives", which the pragmatic-transport line's questions about invariants under admissible transformation ([QUESTION-027](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md), [QUESTION-029](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-029.md), [QUESTION-036](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-036.md)) ask for in the abstract. From five mode-connectivity THEORYs held without links to the line. The carry-over from trained networks to communicative kinds is the filer's, and is the claim's weak point. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) | Fidelity is the wrong measure of a developing argument: maturing drops and changes things legitimately, so what a record can secure is traceability, change that is announced and located, not preservation | The counter to [CLAIM-191](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md), filed with it. The transport line measures fidelity, and [CLAIM-034](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-034.md) already says fidelity is one goal among several. A developing argument aims at maturing, and [TERM-052](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-052.md) says maturing drops things legitimately. A fidelity profile would score legitimate dissolution as distortion. What the record secures is that change is announced and located: traceability. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-191](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md) | Restating an argument across memoryless sessions is iterated transport with only a weak channel back to the source: without anchors, restatements drift toward the collaborators' own framings rather than at random, and a code restores continuity of transmission | The first claim joining the nucleating-argument and pragmatic-transport lines, which shared no edges. A sequence of memoryless sessions restating an argument is a chain of retellings, the telephone game of [CASE-015](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-015.md). The transport line's results then predict that drift has a direction, toward the transmitters' prior ([THEORY-155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md), [CLAIM-090](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-090.md)), and that convergence is not preservation ([CLAIM-081](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-081.md)). A code supplies [CLAIM-002](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s continuity of transmission. Proposed from a synthesis review; the counter is [CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-192](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-192.md) v2 | A multi-session argument's thesis can move without any participant arguing for the move, which is a case of an organized whole's course coming apart from its members' intentions | Links the nucleating-argument line to the distributed-agency line. The translation exchange's thesis moved from [CLAIM-017](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-017.md) to [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) to [CLAIM-133](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-133.md) with no turn arguing either move ([CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md)). [CLAIM-030](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md) says an organized whole's operative intention can evolve apart from what its members intend. The owner, the assistant sessions and the record make up such a whole, and its thesis moved that way. [CLAIM-186](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md)'s test is an intervention test of both. Proposed from the synthesis review; the owner's memory and veto are the main reason to doubt it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-193](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-193.md) v4 | A linear probe family can tell apart only realizations whose representations differ in normalized kernel, and kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed: any distinction beyond that is supplied by the analyst | A partial answer to [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) for the linear case, from THEORYs the record held without linking them to the line. What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of the normalized kernel ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)); kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed (THEORY-004, THEORY-723); an inner product beyond that is a stipulation ([THEORY-018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md)); and spectral degeneracy does not identify the symmetry ([THEORY-019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md)). Proved results for learned representations; the carry-over to communicative realizations is the filer's. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) | A person's roles in contexts that do not meet cannot contradict one another: role conflict needs an overlap, which segregating audiences prevents and collapsed contexts create | The MoM manuscript models a person's roles ("daughter", "teacher", "friend") as sections over family, professional and social contexts, with identity as their global section, failing when the roles contradict. Roles in contexts that do not meet glue ([CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)), so contradiction between them is not yet a failure. Conflict needs an overlap: an occasion on which two audiences are present at once. People manage the cover. They segregate audiences, which keeps the contexts disjoint, and they script the occasions where audiences must meet. Broadcast and networked media collapse contexts, which creates overlaps the person did not choose (boyd 2008, after Meyrowitz 1985). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-198](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md) | Preference reversal is not yet disunity: interests that govern a choice at disjoint times glue, and a self is divided over a choice only on an overlap, which the agent's prediction of its own later valuation creates | Take an agent's interests as sections over contexts of choice, each governing the windows of time in which its valuation ranks first. If the windows do not overlap, the sections glue ([CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)): someone who prefers the diet in the morning and the cake at night is a time-indexed preference, not a divided self. Division needs an overlap, a choice on which both interests bear at once. On Ainslie's account that overlap is made by recursive self-prediction: the present choice is valued as a forecast of the later ones, so the later interest's valuation enters the present context. That is where intertemporal bargaining happens, and it is the coupling [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) found missing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) | Over a fixed scenario, a change of global compatibility at small local distortion needs contextual judgements, which the behavioural data read so far lack; the form of the headline those data leave open is a change of cover, in which a rendering makes some of the source's questions undecidable for its readers and decides others the source left open | The record's narrowing, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md) after [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md). It concedes that the record's reading of [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) finds no contextual behavioural data, so the fixed-scenario form of "Translation may preserve local meanings while changing the global structure of meaning" has no case but a constructed one. It shows why the fixed-scenario form is sharp and why it needs contextuality. It keeps the form the record already names: "Only a change of scenario can make it jump" ([CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)), and manuscript §11's "A transport may preserve overlaps but change the available measurement cover". A proposal; its test is the discriminating study. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-202](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md) | What the line adds to functional and relevance-theoretic accounts of translation is measured structure beyond a static pragmatic profile: the context-indexed profile, its response to later framings and its decision relevance predict receivers' recovery beyond the similarity of static stance and footing ratings | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md). [CLAIM-023](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-023.md) places the line's contribution in "a specified, testable account of which communicative distinctions a translation preserves", so the test of that contribution must be against the accounts that already hold the pragmatic point. This restores [CASE-005](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-005.md)'s three-way selection (semantic, static pragmatic and trajectory similarity), which was gone by A52, with human receivers. A proposal, untested. It does not say the functionalist rivals are wrong. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) v3 | A communicative kind's identity is grounded in its relational organization, for which competent participants' uptake is the standard; statistical methods recover aspects of it from restricted observations; translation transports it; and what persists is what the receivers can still recover, of which the analyst can certify the independently identifiable part | The record's restatement, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) after the audit's objections to it ([CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md), [CLAIM-246](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md), [CLAIM-211](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md)). It keeps the four clauses, adds [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md)'s standard to the first and [CLAIM-223](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md)'s reading to the fourth, and replaces the third defeat disjunct ("no relational structure beyond the observed response profiles is needed", which [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md) showed is always met or undecidable) with an observable comparison on transfer. It supersedes [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md), by the owner's delegated ruling of 2026-10-29. A proposal, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-205](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-205.md) v2 | Functional and relevance-theoretic accounts of translation need not fix one context or a static stance profile, so their strongest operationalization is a rich contextual baseline of context-response profiles and supervised prediction | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12. It accepts [CLAIM-202](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md) as the line's principal empirical thesis and objects to its rival set. Open: no study has been run, and the strong baseline is not specified beyond the reading's table. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md) | If a communicative kind can outrun every probe, human same-kind judgements, themselves one probe family, can neither confirm nor defeat the October thesis; if it cannot, the kind does in the tests only what an observational class does, which the record's term for a kind says it is not | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens, with one point from the empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The dilemma reaches the epistemic and fidelity clauses [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) says the programme does test, not only the ontological clause its "What it does not say" sets aside. Two defeat conditions misfire under it: [CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md)'s is met trivially if the judges' verdicts count as a probe, and [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s third disjunct is either always met or never decidable. It does not say kinds are unreal, and it is not [CLAIM-150](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md)'s underdetermination of the ontology. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-209](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-209.md) | Probes and statistical models recover only the distinctions identifiable from the relational evidence they are given, and a signature sufficient for a stated family of communicative decisions outside the observed probes can be identified when the full latent factorization is not | The assistant's second thesis at U62 (A240 T2), the positive answer to [QUESTION-027](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md). It has now been asserted four times: A214 §7, A218 (RQ3 and the priority theorem target), A232 (§3.2 and F2) and A240. Filed with [QUESTION-027](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md)'s scope: the unrestricted claim is answered by standard results, so its content is in decisions outside the observed probes. No signature is yet named. A proposal; the owner argued none of it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-212](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-212.md) v3 | Fidelity as a report and fidelity as a re-performance are different decision targets: Blackwell's order compares a rendering with its source as evidence about the source's situation, which both readers decide about, while a rendering that re-performs the act in the target's situation is compared only through a correspondence of situations | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md), which it reconciles rather than refutes. In report fidelity the parameter is the source's situation, common to both readers, so Blackwell's order is defined; the objection's worked case then gets a precise verdict, incomparability, as [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) expects, and a context-aware translator's non-garbling is compared by the order and quantified by [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md). The objection is right about re-performance, where [CLAIM-091](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-091.md)'s compensation lives: there a correspondence of situations is needed ([QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md)). For report tasks the task correspondence is the identity, which removes two of [CLAIM-218](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-218.md)'s points there. A proposal; it does not say which kind of fidelity literary translation aims at. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-213](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-213.md) | A proposed relational kind is a hypothesis about invariance across admissible changes of measurement and context, not an equivalence class under the measurements now available, so realism about kinds gains empirical content as extrapolation to probe families, populations and environments not used to construct them | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12. Proposed and not adopted. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-215](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-215.md) v2 | Communicative kinds are repeatable organizations of relations among participants, norms, commitments and possible consequences, which concrete events realize without being one another, and which kind an event realizes is not exhausted by the intrinsic properties of the expression token | The assistant's first thesis at U62 (A240 T1; A232's first proposition and §2), which splits the ontological clause of the October thesis ([CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)) out from the rest and narrows it. The owner asked how to update the theses and argued none of it. Its first two sentences are [TERM-040](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-040.md)'s definition. Its third is weaker than [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md): an intention-based account meets it too, so it does not tell relational constitution from that rival. The study cannot test it. A proposal. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md) v2 | For a communicative kind, the standard of sufficiency is the uptake of competent participants who know the standings and norms in play: a defeasible standard, overridden only where the act's other constituents diverge from the judges' verdicts, so a probe family is tested against it, and a kind outruns the families coarser than that standard and the judges only through those constituents | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), and the argument [CLAIM-247](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-247.md) found missing. Calling a probe family insufficient ([CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), [CLAIM-135](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-135.md)) presupposes a standard beyond it. For an act partly constituted by uptake ([CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md)), competent participants' uptake is that standard, and since version 2 a defeasible one: CLAIM-241 is conceded, so the verdicts yield where the act's other constituents diverge from them. The kind's extension is the class the standard fixes, and analysts' families are insufficient when coarser. No test needs a kind that outruns every family. A proposal, resting on a Proposed premise. It does not touch [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s ontological clause, which the programme does not test. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md) v2 | For a named population of receivers and a stated family of tasks, what survives a translation, retelling or rendering is the set of task-relevant communicative distinctions those receivers can still recover from it, and measured preservation of the pragmatic observables predicts that recovery better than preservation of the wording or of the proposition, with or without its force | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the audit's objections to the tests of the manuscript's thesis ([CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md), [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md), [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md)). It restates [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) as an empirical claim indexed to receivers and tasks, tested against the rival [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) itself names, a proposition with its force, on a behavioural criterion and with an interlingual arm that decides. It supersedes [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md), by the owner's delegated ruling of 2026-10-29. It is a proposal, not a finding. It does not claim the line's distinctive machinery is needed: that is [CLAIM-202](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-221](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md) | The relational-constitution thesis's defeat condition describes a standard rival the record holds no counter for, intention-based accounts of illocution, which plausibly meet it for every act in the four-speakers case except the institutional one | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) is defeated by a held account that individuates teasing, reproach and reprimand by the utterance plus speaker-internal states. That is the intention-based line of Grice, Strawson and Bach and Harnish, none of whom the record holds. On it [CASE-018](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-018.md)'s friend, parent and comedian differ in communicative intention, and only the judge needs norms, which Searle ([LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) already supplies. The record's own model for [CLAIM-111](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md) is of this family. The objection is open; it would narrow [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) to institutional acts unless an argument from uptake meets it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-224](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md) | Under partial relational constitution, a translation always changes the participants, audience and norms that the relational-constitution thesis makes constituents of the act, so whether the act survives turns on a correspondence of relations the structure cannot supply from inside | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A translation is addressed to a new audience under new norms, so on [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) it changes constituents of the act, and the record's way out is always a correspondence ("the appropriate relationships", "corresponding relational organizations"). That makes [QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) a question about what the act is, not only how to measure it, and the record's model of translation holds the audience fixed. [CLAIM-138](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-138.md) spares [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md); this applies its point to [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) through translation. The objection is open. It does not say acts never survive translation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md) v4 | D_obs restated over a rendering procedure, with one kernel family fitted on some source items and scored on held-out ones and the target term the readers' response averaged over the procedure's output, separates rendering procedures that receivers' task-indexed recovery separates, so restated it measures observational fidelity informatively | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, of the manuscript's L_obs and the profile's D_obs after [CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md), [CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) and [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md). For one pair a constant kernel makes D_obs zero ([CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md)); fixed across items, it fits only if the target readers' responses do not vary with the item. The repair ties the outcome-level kernels to the text channel, makes the transport a property of a procedure ([CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md)), and makes deficiency a finite computation over judgement outcomes ([CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md)). A proposal: the derivation is elementary, but whether the restated measure is informative is the defeat condition's empirical question. It does not say a fitted kernel is the translator's process. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-240](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-240.md) v3 | A holistic fidelity judgement is fidelity under the judges' default task, a weighting of the profile's components that can be estimated on some renderings and tested on others, so it is well defined and consistent with task-relativity, and a defeat condition that uses it must name the population and fix the weighting before the test, and across populations with unequal access to the source must fit the weighting only on the components each can perceive | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md). Task-relativity ([CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md)) denies a ranking that holds across tasks, not that a population has a default task. A weighting estimated on held-in data and tested on held-out data is a finding, not a fit, and a weighting fixed before the test leaves no room to blame the task after a failure. A proposal: whether holistic judgements are such a weighting is itself empirical. The objection is right that the stated defeat conditions name neither task nor receivers; [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md), [CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) and [QUESTION-075](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-075.md) address that. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-242](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-242.md) v3 | The use-level counterpart of Saussure's value is an utterance's contrast with the alternatives its speaker could have used in context; values do not cross between languages, which is why fidelity is graded transport through an anchored correspondence rather than identity of value | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-254](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-254.md). It grants the objection's premises: value is internal to one language state, and it is a fact of langue, while the line's observables are facts of use. It denies the conclusion. What the premise rules out is identity of value across languages, which the line does not claim ([CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)), and transport through a correspondence fixed from outside both systems is what [CLAIM-082](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md)'s own qualification already requires. At the level of use, contrast with alternatives is the rational-speech-act model's premise ([THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md)) and Bergen, Goodman and Levy's finding ([LIT-809](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-809.md)). Saussure becomes precedent, not premise. A proposal, not a refutation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md) v2 | The defeat tests take one holistic, task-free judgement of fidelity as ground truth, though the line's own theses say fidelity is task-relative, interpreter-relative and not a single ranking | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A judge asked "how faithful?" or "the same kind?" supplies an unstated task and weighting, and is one interpreter. The theory's measure must then be fitted to that weighting, which is circular, or a mismatch blamed on the judges' task, which leaves nothing that defeats. It does not say the judgements are useless, only that the defeat conditions lack the task and receiver index the line's own theses say fidelity needs. [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) is its neighbour: that one moves the criterion to the analyst, and neither says it is task-free. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-250](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) | What a developing argument should preserve through legitimate revision is its accountability structure, what was asserted, why, how it was challenged and what justified its revision, not its propositions, so fidelity is defined over justificatory and provenance relations while propositional content changes | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the third open tension ([CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) against [CLAIM-252](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-252.md)). It reads the tension as mostly reconcilable and moves the fidelity object from propositions to justificatory relations. Proposed and not adopted. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-251](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-251.md) v2 | A change in which questions a receiver population can answer determinately is not by itself a change of cover in the sheaf sense: the cover belongs to the measurement scenario and the responses are an empirical model on it, so such a change is a change of empirical model, which can create or remove a gluing obstruction on a fixed cover but does not change what the cover is, and the operational notion needs its own name until a functorial link is shown | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the open tension between [CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) with [CASE-048](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-048.md) and the operational cover of [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md). It keeps the empirical notion and denies it the sheaf-theoretic name. Open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-255](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-255.md) v2 | Intending to perform an act, performing it and being recognized as having performed it are distinct, coupled variables: intended meaning is fixed at production, the act partly by roles, standing and norms, and recognition by uptake, so competent uptake is constitutive for some acts, evidential for others and irrelevant to the existence of still others | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the first open tension ([CLAIM-160](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-160.md) against [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md)). It gives each claim its own object rather than picking one. Proposed and not adopted: the owner has not taken it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md) v2 | Blackwell's order compares experiments about one parameter, so it does not reach the normal translation case: source and target readers decide about situations with changed coordinates, and where the state is common a translator with context knowledge yields a rendering that is not a garbling of the source, which the order typically leaves incomparable with it and about which the direction the manuscript uses is silent | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange states it. [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s comparison is over one state Z. Compensation ([CLAIM-091](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-091.md)) changes the social coordinates, so the target reader decides about a different situation. Where the situation is common, a translator who knows the context makes a rendering that depends on Z other than through the source, so it is not a garbling. Blackwell's order is still defined then, but typically leaves source and target incomparable, and the direction the manuscript uses says nothing. It does not say decision-relative fidelity is wrong. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-262](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-262.md) v2 | Whether an agent's regimes are coordinated by discrete switches or by continuous reorganization depends on how the agent is constituted; both occur | The owner's answer to [QUESTION-079](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-079.md): both forms are possible, and which one an agent shows depends on its constitution. An agent made of a population whose choices accumulate like a drift-diffusion process reorganizes continuously. Twitch Plays Pokémon approximates one, best in democracy mode with the tally visible as votes arrive. The consequence for [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md)'s transition test is that it must be stated per constitution. A missing switch counts against coordination only in an agent built to switch. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-263](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-263.md) v3 | Whether two trained networks compute the same way can be tested by quotienting the architecture's full symmetry group and measuring what remains: a barrier that survives alignment marks a different mechanism, connection after alignment means shared feature structure, and the test cannot run where features have no counterpart | The general content of [CLAIM-187](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-187.md), filed alone in learned-structure under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md): a measured protocol for asking whether two trained solutions are the same solution. Quotient the full symmetry group, including the orthogonal map on a transformer's residual stream ([THEORY-112](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-112.md)). Read a barrier that survives as a difference of mechanism ([THEORY-116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-116.md)). Between linearly connected image classifiers, nearly every layer's features interpolate ([THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)). The test cannot run where features have no counterpart ([THEORY-113](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-113.md)) or the objectives share no structure ([THEORY-115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-115.md)). It is the first claim in the learned-structure line. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-271](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-271.md) v2 | A collective's reasons need not be any of its members' reasons, so aggregating members' conclusions, as polling does, can yield verdicts the collective's own reasons do not support | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-13, given in conversation by refining "the good of a higher level agent need not align with the respective goods of the parts" to reasons. The assistant drew the polling consequence. On [THEORY-725](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-725.md) a group that judges linked propositions must choose between aggregating premises and aggregating conclusions, and the two can disagree. A poll aggregates conclusions. It does not say that polling is illegitimate, nor that the collective knows better than its members. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md) v2 | Participation on a shared canvas thins selectively: people keep coming back while art they invested in survives, so unaffiliated corruption falls over the event and the remaining participants are weighted toward maintainers, a cooling schedule the population produces for itself | The owner's correction to [CLAIM-273](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-273.md). Over days, random participation is a real decay, and it is not constant. Uninvested participants drop out, and invested ones stay while their art persists, which "creat[es] a survival function that biases towards user's sustaining participation if the art they are invested in persists". So the "temperature" of random corruption is high early and low late. This is a feedback from pattern to flow, and it answers [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) in part. Untested on the logs. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-276](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-276.md) v2 | A shared interpretation's coherence, its fidelity to evidence and the plurality of live alternatives are separate quantities, and a population can raise the first while lowering the other two, so a collective interpretation's stability is no evidence of its truth | A1 §6, before the influence canvas: meaning as "metastable patterns of mutually reinforcing constraints", with the caveat that "delusions, dogmas, and self-reinforcing errors can also become metastable". So coherence C(M), evidential fidelity F(M, Y) and plurality P(M) must be measured apart. Zollman's result that sparser communication helps a community settle on the better option ([THEORY-143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-143.md)) and Holman and Bruner's industrial selection ([THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md)) are the record's readings that bear on it. It does not say coherence is bad. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-281](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-281.md) v2 | Endorsement indexed by role lets a process empower another as a critic while opposing its preferred policy, so an organization that allocates authority by role can keep disagreement working inside it instead of sorting into factions | A2 §8, on the owner's U2 design. If processes endorse only those whose policies match their own, the influence structure "risks degenerating into factions of mutually reinforcing beliefs". Indexing endorsement by role, E_i(j, r, c, t), lets i back j as an error detector without backing j's authority over the final choice. [CASE-080](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-080.md) is the worked example. It does not say role boundaries hold under pressure. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md) v3 | An endorsement scheme that denies each operator control over its own authority can make delegation do work: rewarded for how far their preferred policies are realized and not for authority held, operators delegate to aligned others, and the two conditions need not be confined to one-hop allocation | The owner's design at U2 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: operators vote on one another's influence, cannot significantly manipulate their own, and gain by finding aligned operators and delegating authority to them. A2 made it precise. Two conditions are imposed: each operator's own authority is insensitive to its own endorsements, and its payoff is how closely the collective decision matches what it would endorse. Under them, empowering a better-placed ally is a way to get one's policies realized without becoming more powerful. It does not say such schemes resist collusion, or that alignment makes delegation wise. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-286](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-286.md) v2 | Habit, akrasia, rumination, rigidity and insight can be modelled as regimes of one organization, in which processes transform shared meaning and allocate one another's influence, with trust, specialization and higher-level agency arising from its history and not imposed | A7's central thesis, the explanatory half of the manuscript, kept apart from the constitutive half ([CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md)) as A7 itself asked. Its novelty is the unification, not any ingredient: "multi-agent cognition, competing control systems, temporal discounting, self-exciting processes, and organizational emergence all have substantial literatures". It is the claim [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) objects to. It does not say these processes are a self. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-295](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-295.md) v2 | A record of an inquiry's justifications adds nothing for decisions its current state already suffices for: what it can add is a wider family of decisions for which what is kept suffices, and decisions a bounded agent can make that it otherwise could not | A10's conclusion, with A5's second claim and A10 §5's three values of history: informational, computational and option value. It places [CLAIM-250](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) without settling it. [CLAIM-250](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) says what accountable inquiry ought to preserve; this says what preserving it could buy. The cases make the first half exact ([CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md), [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md)). The second half, that real inquiries change their questions in ways that make the purchase worth its cost, is not shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) v2 | A frame can change a judgement by changing which of an interpreter's stored distinctions are reachable, without supplying any evidence about what is being judged | A20's proposed claim, after the owner tied addressing to anchoring at U20, and A19's "addressing conditions". Its psychological form is the selective-accessibility account of anchoring, and the readings of 2026-10-15 weaken it: Strack and Mussweiler (1997, read) infer accessibility from moderations and latencies without measuring it, and their model lets the same retrieved knowledge push a judgement either way; Harris et al. (2019, read) find the most direct measure of the accessibility step does not replicate and cannot detect priming at all. The retrieval step is inferred, not shown. The mechanism the record holds, attention as sparse distributed memory ([LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md)), is a model, not evidence about judges. The extension to communication in general is the record's and is not shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-301](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-301.md) v2 | Iterative retrieval can turn a provisional interpretation into a premise: a framing selects what is encountered, what is encountered reinforces the framing, and the question being investigated drifts as well as the queries | A21's proposed claim, from the owner's U21 link between retrieval-mediated anchoring, agent harnesses and older information retrieval. Classical IR named query drift ([LIT-1079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1079.md)). An agent that rewrites its own task adds [TERM-056](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-056.md), which A21 judged "arguably more consequential". The exchange did this itself between A2 and A13. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md) | Filing an argument moves work across time: it is paid for now, in filing, indexing, tracking dependencies and checking it is still current, against reconstruction later, so it is worth its cost only when expected reuse covers it, and recurrence is evidence of reuse, not the criterion | A11, at the owner's request for "content to the effect of computation-storage tradeoffs". A11's four expenditures (materialization, indexing, dependency tracking, refresh) and its break-even condition. The arithmetic is trivial. The thesis is about the record: that its second-occurrence rule ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)) and the nucleation threshold of [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) are approximations to this trade, and can fail in both directions. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) v3 | Where reuse cannot be forecast, recurrence weighted by reconstruction cost is the filing criterion, not only evidence for one: filing at the first use at which reconstructing again would take the overpayment past the cost of filing is within 2 − (c_a + u)/c_r of the hindsight optimum on every sequence of uses, at most twice, and no deterministic rule without foresight guarantees materially better, under fixed known costs, with staleness left out and the cost of recognizing what a filed argument answers taken as fixed | Filed at the owner's request, from the rent-or-buy result of Karlin et al. 1988 ([THEORY-348](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-348.md)) set against [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s clause that recurrence is evidence of reuse, not the criterion. In [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s own terms the break-even rule needs no forecast and is worst-case optimal; [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)'s second-occurrence rule is that rule when filing costs about one reconstruction. It does not reach staleness, which the theorem forbids rather than prices, or drifting costs, and where reuse can be forecast an expected-reuse rule can do better, so [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s criterion survives there. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-314](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-314.md) | Reusing a filed argument has a recognition cost that a fixed per-use price leaves out: certifying that stored answers cover a new question is NP-complete even for conjunctive queries, grows with the number and size of the stored definitions rather than being a constant per item, and is undefined for an item filed without a statement of what it answers, so each filing raises the cost of later reuse and per-item break-even decisions are not independent | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on answering queries using views (Levy, Mendelzon, Sagiv and Srivastava 1995; Chandra and Merlin 1977; Halevy 2001). [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md)'s guarantee needs a fixed, known per-use cost c_a; recognizing that a stored answer covers a new question is a search whose cost depends on everything stored, so filing one item changes the price of using the others. It undermines the premise [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) states, not its arithmetic. The hardness is worst case and over short definitions, partial reuse is cheap, and nothing here is measured on the record. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-315](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-315.md) | In comparative anchoring tasks, considering an anchor shifts the later numerical estimate without adding evidence about the target, and the shift is carried by anchor-consistent knowledge made more accessible; the shift is established, the accessibility step is inferred and has not been measured | The empirical half of [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md), split off under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md)'s pilot, which found that claim compound: an empirical claim about judgement tasks and an interpretive extension to communication in general. This half is scoped to the comparative-question paradigm. Its first part is established ([THEORY-337](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-337.md)); its second is the selective-accessibility account ([THEORY-335](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md)), whose direct test failed to replicate with a measure that also missed direct priming. [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) now rests on it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-317](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-317.md) v2 | Self-presentations that differ by audience do no harm while the audiences are kept apart; people keep them apart and script the occasions where they must meet, and broadcast and networked media bring them together unchosen, which is when the presentations collide | Split from [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical half of that claim, the sociology of audiences on which its sheaf reading rests. Its evidence is boyd (2008, read in part in [NOTE-710](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-710.md)), after Meyrowitz (1985), and one documented collapse, [CASE-064](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-064.md). boyd's claims about collapse are documented with interviews and examples, not measured, and the Carmichael case reaches the record secondhand, so it stays Proposed. It says nothing about overlaps, covers or gluing; that is [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md)'s. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md) | A slowly changing collective variable, such as a reputation, a rivalry or a standing, is part of a collective's dynamics and not only an observer's average when its members read it, condition what they do on it, and by doing so regenerate it | A9 §3 and §10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, after Flack 2012 (LIT-1122, unread). Three stages: an observer finds a stable statistic of fast interactions; members recognize it and use it; their use preserves or regenerates it. Only the third makes the variable an endogenous level. It is the general form of [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md), where trust is the temporal regularity of endorsement that then steers endorsement. It does not say that such a variable individuates one collective: five slow variables sharing a referent may be five processes. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-329](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md) v5 | A collective that replaces all its members persists, when it does, by causal transmission of the organization that produces it, not by resemblance: an organization of the same kind that arises independently is not its continuation, and a lapse in its coherence need not end it | A5, A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A9 §9 separated three persistences that dissociate: state persistence (a variable changes slowly), dynamical persistence (characteristic responses continue) and historical persistence (the producing processes are transmitted and reconstituted across successive populations). A5: "a system's ability to reproduce itself as the same kind is not automatically sufficient for its numerical persistence as the same individual." The second time the record meets "causal-organizational continuity": [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) noted A10 §4.3's of 2026-10-13 and did not file it. It does not say what must be transmitted, or settle branching successors. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-332](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-332.md) v2 | A loosely organized population can change what an outside institution does through its members' separately motivated acts of making, selecting and passing things on, without forming a collective intention or judgment, when the organized pattern of those acts, and not only the acts of identifiable individuals, earns its place in explaining the change | A7's "distributed cultural uptake", of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on the owner's Juggernaut case. | [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) v2 | The selectivity active inference gives action, sampling what one expects to experience, is played in the coupled meaning–authority model by the authority space: influence decides which operators retrieve and so what the next judgement observes, which makes Friston's self-confirming sampling the model's authority-to-interpretation arrow and his agent a coupled loop run without independent scoring | The owner's, U10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on Friston et al.'s "sampling selectively what one expects to experience": "I think this selectivity maps to the authority space in my coupled model." | [CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md) v2 | Freedom of will and autonomy come in degrees along several dimensions, among them viable reachability, control cost, robustness to disturbance, governance reconfigurability, revisability and motivational integration, and agents compare by inclusion of what they can viably reach under matched conditions: a partial order with incomparable pairs, not a scalar, and a gradient only of a declared measure | The owner's, U9 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "controllability of a system isn't binary, and neither is sensitivity to perturbation", so can the account speak of "gradations (perhaps even gradients/spectra?) of freedom of will/autonomy". | [CLAIM-355](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md) v6 | In a distributed agent the binding of appraisal, readiness and governance into one response can be real while the single owner a self-model or collective self-description attributes it to is a representational construction, not a further entity; the illusion, where there is one, is in the attribution and belongs to whichever system adopts the representation, and this deflates the self without settling whether experience is real | The owner's, U26 and U27 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: at U26 whether, "adopting an illusionist/fictionalist position", the record can make claims about subjecthood; at U27, "illusory binding-type phenomena in distributed agents", starting from the record's emotion material. | [CLAIM-358](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-358.md) v3 | Learned local accommodation can reduce the amortized cost of recurrent arbitration: where a recurring conflict among an agent's processes admits a stable accommodation, settling it among the processes can cost less over repeated encounters than escalating each instance to a higher-level process that mediates or overrides, though local negotiation and the relations it needs are not free | The owner's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "processes which can navigate disagreement amongst themselves require fewer resources from the system than processes which need to activate additional subsystems to resolve disagreement." | [CLAIM-361](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-361.md) | Relief of an organization's frustration must be judged for an identified organization against a fixed reference set of its original demands, under an explicit correspondence between earlier and later demands: a demand excised or suppressed has changed the comparison and has not been satisfied, an endogenous revision of what the organization maintains is a transformation of it and not relief, and learning can change which processes bear the demands | The owner's prompt, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's line that deleting a demand "has changed the comparison problem": "it might be helpful to connect back to our notions of individuation". | [CLAIM-362](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-362.md) | Non-domination of an agent's subcomponents is a candidate constituent of authenticity as an organizational achievement, not a sufficient criterion of ownership: higher-level processes need not impose the outcome because the lower-level ones already support it or settle their disagreement among themselves, and a process that rarely decides keeps access to the roles in which it is consequential | The owner's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "'authenticity' should be treated as an organizational achievement characterized by non-domination of subcomponents". | [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md) v4 | Whether a training-time regulatory condition belongs to a network depends on which unit is individuated for the training dynamics and whose jurisdiction governs the updates; in conventional training most of that governance falls to the optimizer–model–data system, so a condition of training is not thereby a condition of the network | The owner's correction, U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "it might help clarify things if we apply our individuation and volition frameworks to this system", the system being a deep network during training (U30). | [CLAIM-393](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-393.md) | Ordinary and legal attributions of agency to an artifact cannot serve as the independent marks that would defeat the record's agency test, because they turn on whether its mechanism is understood: a known mechanism invites "This is all just programmed!", an inscrutable one invites fear, whatever the description lengths | From Boyle's "inscrutability paradox" in The Line ([LIT-1288](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1288.md), read in [NOTE-1014](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1014.md)): if an apparently general AI comes from well-understood programming, people will doubt it has autonomous consciousness, since it is "merely doing or saying that which we have programmed it to do"; if its workings are inscrutable, they will find it "more mysterious and potentially more threatening" (p. 30; pp. 54, 246, 272). | [CLAIM-404](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md) v2 | An organization can be governed from outside without any of its decisions being made for it, through the evidence its own procedures receive or through the criteria by which they weigh evidence; the two routes are distinct and each is possible without the other, so informational and evaluative independence do not imply each other; and where the organization's role is to evaluate another that affects its evidence or resources, the interpretation–authority loop can close between the two institutions, so that formal independence of the evaluator's procedure does not make its evaluation independent | The owner's cases, U20 ("maybe cases like reflexive control and regulatory capture could be informative here") and U21 (news-media capture) of the exchange of 2026-10-20, with A26 §4's two constructions and A27 §6. | [CLAIM-417](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) v4 | What the record explained by "self" in its dispositional, persisting, self-governing and integrated senses is better explained by organizational perspectives, with a perspective, its carriers, its lineage and its representations kept apart; the subject sense stays a separate question, and narrative, presented and modeled selves involve representations that may describe a perspective, attribute it to a bearer or construct an owner, none of them the perspective itself | The owner's, at U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the record's earlier "selves" are "better described as 'organizational perspectives'". | [CLAIM-423](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-423.md) v2 | In a political collective, components that change at different speeds (attention, coalitions, elected terms, administrative careers, law and treaties, generational memory) are not only nested by timescale: under a given institutional arrangement their different temporal horizons affect which forms of influence each can accumulate, exercise and keep, and so which of them holds authority over the others, so a state can stay continuous as an actor while the organization producing its positions changes under it | The owner's, at U28 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: domestic and international politics as the domain where "regime ecology" becomes concrete, with "separation of timescales in elections, durations of tenure in elected and appointed positions, lifespan, generational memory, etc." creating "amorphous collectives of varying orders and degrees of coupling". | [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) | A perspective governs itself with respect to social judgement to the extent that it keeps access to others' judgements of it while making their authority over its conduct depend on their grounds, not on their visibility, repetition or attributed plurality; neither absorbing every judgement nor resisting every one meets this, since both let the judgements set the terms of response | A39's closing thesis and its fourth reading of "I am whatever you say I am", in the exchange of 2026-10-22, filed at the owner's request. | [CLAIM-426](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-426.md) v2 | Where a judgement's circulation helps bring about what it says, its visibility, repetition and attributed plurality are evidence about what it will bring about, so the rule that a judgement's authority should come from its grounds and not its visibility holds for judgements of what already is, and not without qualification for judgements of what someone or something will become | The owner, on 2026-10-23, after [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) was filed: "this is reminding me of 'hyperstition'". | [CLAIM-431](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-431.md) v3 | A corporation's functional remorse cannot be told from prudence: any procedure or role duty that makes others' harms its concern was put there for its own ends, reputation, liability or recruitment, so the line between harm as concern and harm as threat, and with it the line between a remorseful and a psychopathic corporation, does not hold, and the clinical word adds nothing to a description of its incentives | The objection to the record's reading of the "institutional psychopath", revised on 2026-10-23 when the reading was revised. | [CLAIM-432](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-432.md) v4 | A corporation can be an agent fit to be held responsible and the bearer of functional affect in Frijda's sense, so psychopathy's affective features can be assigned to it as well as its conduct: it lacks remorse, functionally, when harm it does to others is not among the concerns its own appraisals track and gains precedence over what it does only when a regulator or a market turns it into a threat to the corporation's concerns; that profile, threat without remorse, is the construct's, and it is changed by redesigning the corporation's concerns, not its members' characters | The record's reading of Bakan's "institutional psychopath" (LIT-1430, unread), filed at the owner's request on 2026-10-23 and revised the same day when the owner pointed out that the record's framework assigns affect to corporation-like things ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md), reopened). A harm to others reaches its decisions either as one of its own concerns (procedures, role duties: functional concern and remorse) or as a threat to its other concerns (regulators, markets: functional fear). | [CLAIM-433](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-433.md) v2 | The potential account of valence is an account of goal-conduciveness valence, not of intrinsic pleasantness: on the component process model's separation of levels of valence, the ordering that prevails ranks states by need satisfaction and goal attainment, the potential's strength tracks 'wanting' and its sign tracks goal conduciveness, while 'liking' is a separate appraisal with its own ordering; so the wanting–liking dissociation is two valence systems coming apart, as that separation predicts, and the objection that the account is not about pleasure is conceded rather than answered | The reply the owner asked for, 2026-10-23, to the objection that potential tracks 'wanting', not 'liking' ([CLAIM-438](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-438.md)). Shuman, Sander and Scherer's "levels of valence" separate intrinsic pleasantness from goal conduciveness, on Berridge's evidence; Scherer and Moors report that the two have different physiological signatures and combine multiplicatively. The record's ordering is goal conduciveness. | [CLAIM-435](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-435.md) v2 | Veit's common currency and ALARM's override are two regimes of one ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, compensatory and overriding, so their rivalry over what the first felt valence did becomes the question whether the earliest potential orderings are continuous: in motivational trade-off experiments, a continuous indifference curve between a noxious cost and a resource for Veit, a discontinuity at a threshold beyond which no resource buys the cost for ALARM; only a graded override, deciding at every level of its own intensity, lacks a currency altogether | A consequence of the owner's reframing of valence as ordering-potential ([CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)). It is recast instead: both are an ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, compensatory or overriding, and the trade-off test separates them by continuity. Corrected on reading Debreu before filing: a threshold override still has a (discontinuous) currency; only a graded override has none ([CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md), part 3a). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-437](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-437.md) v3 | 'Wanting' and 'liking' are saliences relative to different, overlapping processes, pursuit and consummation, each ranking states by their bearing on its own concerns; valence is then relative to a perspective, every perspective in the negotiation has its own, the system's valence is that of the perspective whose ordering is the negotiation's potential, and ambivalence is strong saliences of opposite sign with no potential absorbing them | The owner's, 2026-10-23: "maybe 'wanting' and 'liking' can be differentiated by characterizing them as saliencies relative to different (possibly overlapping) processes? | [CLAIM-438](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-438.md) v4 | An ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, as the potential account of valence defines it, tracks 'wanting', not 'liking': sensitized incentive salience wins a system's conflicts, persists and resumes while hedonic impact measured by taste reactivity stays flat or falls, so the regime the account calls hedonic valence is motivational valence, and hedonic valence, if it is anywhere in the account, is elsewhere | Raised by the reading of Berridge and Kringelbach ([NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md)) filed on 2026-10-23 for the potential account. | [CLAIM-439](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-439.md) v2 | A regime of valence is felt, in the sense of attended and available to the system's other processes, when the system that is in it also models it: when a deeper process infers which ordering wins its negotiation, which way the system is moving along it and how strongly it prevails, and the inference is used elsewhere in the system; unfelt valence is the potential without that model, as unfelt fluency is a change in precision without the inference about it | Filed at the owner's direction, 2026-10-23, as a candidate for when the functional regime of [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) is felt.
